chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Abbas ibn Aamir, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khash'ami, from Zurays ibn Abdul Malik, who said:

When it reached Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that a man got married during a time of heat at midday, so Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not see the two of them as being concordant'. So they ended up being separated.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the time of day for marriage in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Imam’s intuitive discernment (kashf) regarding the psychological and physical effects of environmental conditions on marital harmony, specifically linking the intensity of midday heat to potential discord. It serves as a foundational text in Shia jurisprudence for evaluating 'time' (waqt) as a factor in the validity and success of marriage contracts, emphasizing that external circumstances can influence internal compatibility.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Al Abbas Bin Aamir, from Muhammad Bin Yahya Al Khash’amy, from Zurays Bin Abdul Malik who said,

‘When it reached Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> that a man got married during a time of heat at midday, so Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not see the two of them as being concordant’. So they ended up being separated’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hassan ibn Ali from al-‘Abbas ibn ‘Amir and Muhammad ibn Yahya al- Khath’amiy from Durays ibn ‘Abd al-Malik who has said the following:

“When it was mentioned to abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that a man married a woman during the heat of the midday, abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘I do not see they can agree.’ They then separated from each other (as he (the Imam) had mentioned).’”
